transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-21
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 66 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Jason Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood Product), Alex Chen (BridgeScale CTO), Maya Patel (Eng Manager), Samir Rao (SRE), Erin Lee (Security)

Summary:
Quick demo focused on streaming liveness under burst traffic, long-context behavior (50k token-ish use case), and how Redwood's Console/Optimize suggestions interact with throughput and backpressure. Customer wanted to validate Hosted vs Dedicated tradeoffs and confirm telemetry for audit/SOC2.

Topics covered:
- Burst simulator run and how it triggers streaming backpressure fallback
- Long context KV-cache hit/miss effects on latency and memory
- TTLs and session eviction policies in Console
- Quantization and batching recommendations from Optimize
- Security controls (KMS, audit logs, SSO) and data residency

Action items (recorded in call):
- Run extended burst sim with their prompt set
- Share SOC2 + KMS integration doc and private deployment options
- Pricing for a month-long Dedicated pilot with burst buffer capacity

Transcript:
[00:00] Jason: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm Jason, AE on the account, and Priya is our SE who'll walk through the simulator and the console.
[00:12] Alex: hey Jason, hi Priya, thanks. we got a packed agenda. we're most worried about the voice assistant's 40k–60k context windows and then sudden spikes at holiday launches.
[00:22] Priya: cool, yeah we'll show both long context behavior and a synthetic burst we run from the Console. we'll also point out what Optimize recommends for batching and quant profiles.
[00:31] Maya: quick qual question — are you expecting us to go Dedicated for the pilot or can we do Hosted with burst buffer?
[00:38] Jason: good question. short answer: you can start Hosted but with predictable bursts Dedicated gives better latency SLOs and isolation. there are tradeoffs on cost.
[00:48] Samir: cost and SLOs — do you have real numbers? like p50/p95 for hosted under a 5000 rps burst for a 4k token response vs dedicated?
[01:03] Priya: i have an example — it's in the Console demo. but high-level: Hosted uses smart routing and fallback to a smaller quantized variant when queues fill, so p95 can climb. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools so tail latency stays stable, we can show numbers.
[01:18] Erin: and from security, SAML SSO and KMS — can you confirm where keys live for Hosted?
[01:25] Jason: Hosted can integrate customer KMS via our keywrap flow, but for full control Private deployment/VPC keeps keys entirely customer-managed. we'll attach the KMS doc after.
[01:36] [00:60] Priya: ok i'm sharing my screen — Console > Experiments > Burst simulator. i'm going to load BridgeScale's anonymized prompt profile (sample) and run the 10-minute burst at 5k rps to show the state transitions.
[02:10] Alex: slight audio delay here, but i'm seeing the graph. what's that orange line?
[02:17] Priya: that's queue depth. blue is throughput, green is avg latency. notice at minute 2 the KV cache starts getting evictions, we have a spike to 1.2s avg — that correlates to cold kv hits.
[02:32] Maya: the KV cash — excuse me — kv cache — are those per-session or global?
[02:36] Priya: they're shard-local but we present them as logical per-customer caches. we can tune TTLs per route in the Console; Optimize will recommend a TTL based on access patterns.
[02:49] Samir: when the KV cache evicts and latency spikes, what fallback happens for streaming? do you buffer or chunk tokens?
[02:58] Priya: Redwood's streaming runtime does continuous batching and if the backpressure exceeds the burst buffer threshold, we switch to chunked generation with per-chunk ACKs. that keeps connections alive but increases perceived latency.
[03:12] Alex: so chunked generation will still stream tokens but slower, right? we worry about liveness — users disconnecting if tokens lag for >2s.
[03:20] Priya: correct, that's why we demoed the liveness policy. you can set a minimal token heartbeat and fallback to a shorter model variant to keep token heartbeat under 200ms.
[03:32] [03:45] Jason: quick interruption — previously you mentioned smaller quantized variants — do those change output quality? we have regression sensitivity tests.
[03:52] Priya: they can. Optimize will suggest when to use a quantized variant and surface evaluation deltas on your prompt set. for BridgeScale's QA set we expect negligible drop for templated responses but could see regression on long-form narratives.
[04:07] Maya: hmm, for our product the narrative style matters. we won't accept hallucinations increasing. what's the rollback story?
[04:14] Priya: rollouts are canary/A-B with automatic rollback based on your eval hooks and quality thresholds in the Console. also you can pin a model version per route.
[04:26] [05:00] Priya: i'm toggling the burst buffer to simulate saturation — notice the system moves requests to a fallback pool. that triggers the Console alert and creates a replay log you can download.
[05:16] Samir: logs — do those include raw prompts?
[05:19] Priya: by default logs are redacted; we support full-text if you opt-in and sign the data policy. there's also field-level redaction and PII masking hooks.
[05:30] Erin: ok, audit logs for SOC2 evidence — are they immutable? can we forward to our SIEM?
[05:36] Jason: yes, audit trails are append-only and we have integrations to forward to Splunk/Datadog and S3 for long-term retention.
[05:43] [06:00] Priya: now i'll run the long-context run. this is a 50k token conversational session that keeps growing. watch memory usage and kv-hit rate.
[06:15] Maya: timeline on memory — what happens when session exceeds the GPU KV capacity? does Redwood truncate history?
[06:21] Priya: default is soft-truncate based on relevance scoring; we maintain a sliding window and score chunks, but you can opt-in for full-history offloading to cheap storage with prefetch. that's part of the private deployment play.
[06:35] Alex: would that prefetch add cold-start latency for old segments?
[06:40] Priya: yes, slightly — Optimize can recommend a prefetch horizon to balance hit-rates vs latency.
[06:46] [07:00] Jason: can we pause — deep question on telemetry: we need token-level billing and per-route latency histograms for our finance/ops. is that available?
[07:09] Liam: yes, Console exposes token counts, model choices, and per-api-key cost breakdowns. there's an API export for billing pipelines.
[07:19] Maya: how about per-tenant throttling? we have multi-tenant customers with different SLAs.
[07:25] Priya: you can set per-api-key quotas and priority classes. we also support routing policies so high-priority traffic goes to dedicated pools.
[07:35] [08:00] Priya: i'm toggling to the Optimize tab — it shows recommendations: increase batch window to 15ms for throughput vs p95, consider q4_8 quant for the encoder, and TTL 30m for KV for this profile.
[08:19] Samir: q4_8 — does that require model conversion time? how disruptive is a quant swap?
[08:25] Priya: conversion is a one-time step for a model variant. we host multiple quant variants and can route to them. switching in production is via rollout policy. downtime is zero.
[08:36] [09:00] Alex: you mentioned routing fallbacks across regions — if a whole region loses capacity do you failover? what's the cross-region latency penalty?
[09:10] Priya: we do cross-region failover, we prefer warm standbys, but cross-region adds RTT so p95 will increase. Console shows simulated failover impact for your region-to-region RTT.
[09:24] Maya: are there costs for cross-region egress?
[09:27] Jason: yes, egress is billed; we'll show a pricing matrix. for mission-critical apps many customers accept the trade-off.
[09:36] [10:00] Priya: time for a rough live simulation: i'm initiating a 10-minute synthetic burst with mixed long-session and new session traffic. watch the streaming connections and token heartbeats.
[10:13] Alex: seeing a spike, the stream delta widens at t+90s. can you scroll console to the trace?
[10:19] Priya: mmh let me pull traces — here's a few request traces showing chunked fallback at 1:32. notice the connection stayed open even though throughput dropped.
[10:34] Samir: okay, but what about connection churn? do you have auto-reconnect hints for clients?
[10:39] Priya: we surface retry hints and recommended client-side backoff. also we provide SDK patterns for streaming reconnection to re-establish KV context.
[10:50] [11:00] Jason: question for Priya: for our POC can you run this exact profile for 2 hours and export the raw traces and the Optimize suggestions?
[11:08] Priya: yes, we can. i'll include timestamps and the console replay logs.
[11:12] [12:00] Maya: what about end-to-end latency SLOs in SLA? we need a 99th under 800ms for 4k token responses — is that achievable?
[11:24] Priya: on Dedicated with pinned model versions and pre-warmed KV caches it's achievable. Hosted is trickier unless we provision burst buffers and reserved capacity.
[11:34] Erin: on security again — if we go Dedicated in our VPC, do you still see any PII in logs?
[11:41] Jason: Dedicated in VPC with customer-managed KMS keeps logs in your tenancy, but debug-level logs may still contain tokens unless you enable PII scrubbing. we'll provide config.
[11:52] [13:00] Alex: competitive question — have you run similar demos for other vendors? we looked at OpenAI's streaming behavior and it would drop connections without chunked fallback.
[13:09] Priya: yes, we've done comparative tests. Redwood emphasizes graceful degradation rather than hard drops; Optimize helps choose the right fallback that minimizes quality loss.
[13:20] [14:00] Priya: i'm toggling replay — here's an example where Optimize suggests switching to a different batching profile mid-burst which reduced p95 by 30% at cost +12%.
[14:13] Samir: can we tune the cost/latency knob per route?
[14:18] Priya: yes, per-route policy allows you to set cost sensitivity and latency targets. Console will then surface explicit tradeoffs.
[14:27] [15:00] Liam: small aside — Liam from Product here — how reproducible are these sims in customer's environment vs ours?
[15:35] Priya: sims approximate customer patterns but we always recommend a pilot with real traffic; that's why we do a pilot for a week with live traffic shaping.
[15:44] Alex: timeline — we want to pilot before our summer release in mid-May. is that feasible?
[15:50] Jason: yes, feasible. we can kickoff pilot in early April.
[16:00] [16:30] Priya: running through the last part — TTL tuning, eviction thresholds, and fallback model config. i'm adding an example of a canary rollout policy and how Console automates rollback when evals degrade by >2%.
[16:45] Maya: two concerns: our QA team will run long narrative prompts and will fail any change that alters style. will Optimize give us the delta matrix per prompt?
[16:59] Priya: yes, we can attach per-prompt delta in the Optimize report. it's a key feature for your use-case.
[17:10] [17:30] Jason: Security followup — Erin, anything else?
[17:33] Erin: just to confirm: will you provide a KMS integration runbook and SOC2 evidence? also we want example audit logs for a month retention.
[17:45] Jason: will do, we'll attach to the follow up email.
[17:50] [18:00] Alex: ok, last set of items — pricing appetite and pilot size. we think 200k monthly active users, avg 3k tokens, and peaks up to 8k rps over minutes.
[18:09] Jason: noted. we'll produce a Dedicated pilot quote with burst buffer and a Hosted pilot alternative.
[18:16] [19:00] Priya: i'll note that Optimize suggested q4_8 for enc and TTL 30m, but for your narrative alerts we'll pin the full fp16 variant in the pilot.
[19:27] Samir: do you have SDK guidance for streaming reconnection that preserves KV context? we need Node + mobile examples.
[19:34] Priya: yes, we have client SDK patterns for rehydration and we'll share links.
[19:39] [20:00] Jason: wrapping up — recap of next steps and owners. Priya will run 2hr sim, Alex to send prompt set, Jason to send pricing, and Erin to get SOC/KMS docs.
[20:12] Alex: sounds good. one last question — will we get live support during the pilot?
[20:18] Jason: pilot includes SE support and a warroom for the initial 72 hours of the pilot.
[20:24] Maya: ok thanks everyone.
[20:30] [END]

Notes on transcript quality: medium — occasional mis-typed terms (KV cash, Red wood) and minor speaker mislabels. The Console demo produced export artifacts (burst-sim replay, trace logs) referenced above.
